I've been getting into board games like crazy the last few months. During the holidays I probably picked up enough to last me a year. However, I think board games are well worth the investment. Trying to disconnect more from digital media and get back to physical entertainment. I want my kids growing up playing board games rather than Fortnite. To that end what is everyone's favorite game or what are you fixated on right now?

Anachrony is currently the game in itching to play more of. I find the theme of the game to be amazing on top of solid worker placement mechanics.

I like Arkham Horror second edition. I love the theme and the difficulty seems to be just right. I warn you that the rules are pretty convoluted, but once you get used to them it is not a big deal.

Some games you could likely get family play out of are Pandemic and Flashpoint. In Pandemic you work as a group to cure the world of four disease outbreaks, and in Flashpoint you work as a group to rescue people from a house fire. If you like Pandemic, but want to roll dice, look in to Defenders of the Realm. Munchkin, is a decent pick up and play game. Mysterium is picking up a lot of play with us; you may want to look into it.

I really dig deck builders and dungeon crawlers, so Thunderstone Advance is high on my list. The D&D adventure series are really good if you want dungeon crawling without needing a storyteller, otherwise I recommend Descent Second Edition. People seem to really like Betrayal at House on the Hill too, it's more exploration rather than dungeon crawling.
